title_en: Valeo Cleaning Systems Company v. Xiamen Lucas Auto Parts Co., Ltd., Xiamen Fuke Auto Parts Co., Ltd., and Chen Shaoqiang — dispute over infringement of invention patent
ruling_gist_en: I. Functional features refer to technical features that do not directly define the structure, components, steps, conditions, or relationships thereof of the technical solution of the invention, but rather define the structure, components, steps, conditions, or relationships thereof through the function or effect they achieve in the invention-creation. If a technical feature has already defined or implied the specific structure, components, steps, conditions, or relationships thereof of the technical solution of the invention, then even if the technical feature also simultaneously defines the function or effect it achieves, in principle it does not fall within the category of functional features as referred to in Article 8 of the Interpretation (II) of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Patent Infringement Dispute Cases.

full_text_en:
Valeo Wiping Systems Company v. Xiamen Lucas Auto Parts Co., Ltd., Xiamen Fuke Auto Parts Co., Ltd., and Chen Shaoqiang — Dispute over Infringement of Invention Patent

【Ruling Summary】

I. A functional feature refers to a technical feature that does not directly define the structure, composition, steps, conditions, or relationships thereof of the technical solution of an invention, but instead limits the structure, composition, steps, conditions, or relationships thereof through the function or effect achieved by the feature in the invention-creation. If a technical feature has already defined or implied a specific structure, composition, steps, conditions, or relationships thereof of the invention's technical solution, even if that technical feature also simultaneously defines the function or effect it achieves, it shall, in principle, not be considered a functional feature as referred to in Article 8 of the Interpretation (II) of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Patent Infringement Dispute Cases.

II. In a case where a party appeals a judgment of the first instance, if the party filed an application for preservation of conduct during the first instance proceedings, before the case is transferred to the court of second instance, the court of first instance shall have jurisdiction over the preservation application; after the case is transferred to the court of second instance, the court of second instance shall have jurisdiction. If the circumstances are urgent or may cause other damage to the applicant, and the court of second instance cannot render a final judgment within the time limit for processing the preservation application, it shall make a timely decision on the preservation application according to law.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2019) Supreme People's Court IP Civil Final No. 2

Appellants (Defendants at First Instance): Xiamen Lucas Auto Parts Co., Ltd. Domicile: Siming Park, Tong'an Industrial Concentration Zone, Tong'an District, Xiamen City, Fujian Province, People's Republic of China.

Legal Representative: Chen Shaoqiang, General Manager of the Company.
Authorized Litigation Representatives: Chen Qinghua, Lawyer of Fujian Tianheng United Law Firm.
Authorized Litigation Representative: Zhang Chen, Lawyer of Fujian Tianheng United Law Firm.

Appellants (Defendants at First Instance): Xiamen Fuke Auto Parts Co., Ltd. Domicile: Siming Park, Tong'an Industrial Concentration Zone, Xiamen City, Fujian Province, People's Republic of China.

Legal Representative: Wang Shuwu, Chairman of the Board of the Company.
Authorized Litigation Representatives: Chen Qinghua, Lawyer of Fujian Tianheng United Law Firm.
Authorized Litigation Representative: Zhang Chen, Lawyer of Tianheng United Law Firm.

Appellee (Plaintiff at First Instance): Valeo Wiping Systems Company (Valeo Systèmes d'Essuyage). Domicile: Rue Louis Lormand 78320 La Verrière, France.

Authorized Representative: Murielle Khairallah, Director of Intellectual Property of the Company.
Authorized Litigation Representatives: Lin Yi, Lawyer of Fangda Partners, Shanghai.
Authorized Litigation Representative: Liao Tingting, Lawyer of Fangda Partners, Shanghai.

Defendant at First Instance: Chen Shaoqiang, male, born on March 27, 1975, Han nationality, residing in Xiamen City, Fujian Province, People's Republic of China.

In the case concerning the dispute over infringement of invention patent brought by the Appellants Xiamen Lucas Auto Parts Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Lucas Company) and Xiamen Fuke Auto Parts Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Fuke Company) against the Appellee Valeo Wiping Systems Company (hereinafter referred to as Valeo Company) and the Defendant at First Instance Chen Shaoqiang, the Appellants appealed to this Court against the civil judgment (2016) Shanghai 73 Civil First Instance No. 859, which was rendered by the Shanghai Intellectual Property Court on January 22, 2019, concerning the preliminary ruling on the establishment of infringement and the cessation of infringement. This Court accepted the case on February 15, 2019, formed a five-judge panel according to law, and held a public hearing on March 27, 2019. The common authorized litigation representatives of the Appellants Lucas Company and Fuke Company, Chen Qinghua and Zhang Chen, and the authorized litigation representatives of the Appellee Valeo Company, Lin Yi and Liao Tingting, appeared in court for the hearing. The Defendant at First Instance Chen Shaoqiang, having been duly served with a summons, failed to appear in court without justifiable reasons. This Court proceeded with the trial in absentia according to law. The trial of this case has now been concluded.

Lucas Company and Fuke Company appeal requesting: to set aside the original judgment and amend the judgment to reject Valeo Company's claim for an order to immediately cease infringing the invention patent with patent number ZL200610160549.2, titled "Connector for a Vehicle Wiper and Corresponding Connecting Device" (hereinafter referred to as the patent-in-suit). Main facts and reasons:

(I) The original judgment erred in finding that the accused infringing product could be used in the use environment defined by claim 1 of the patent-in-suit, namely, "a connector for a wiper, used to ensure the connection and articulation between a wiper arm and a component of a wiper blade." 1. In the accused infringing product, the wiper arm is connected to the connector, the connector is articulated with the wiper blade component, and there is no direct contact or articulation relationship between the wiper arm and the wiper blade component themselves. 2. Valeo Company's argument that there exists an indirect articulation relationship between the wiper arm and the wiper blade component through the connector in the accused product is untenable. This interpretation violates the principle of primarily using the literal interpretation for patent claims, and the specification does not mention the concept of indirect articulation. The parent application of the patent-in-suit did not disclose that the connector is used to ensure indirect articulation between the wiper arm and the wiper blade component, and the claim for indirect articulation cannot be based on the divisional application.

(II) The original judgment erred in finding that claim 1 of the patent-in-suit does not require the wiper arm to be a "standard wiper arm." In this case, a person skilled in the art, reading the claims and specification of the patent-in-suit, would clearly and reasonably understand that the protected subject matter must use a standard wiper arm and a standard connector. In other words, the width of the wiper arm's locking element and the connector must match; otherwise, the elastic element cannot lock the connector. The accused infringing product is not necessarily used in the specific use environment defined by claim 1 of the patent-in-suit in commerce; it can be used with non-standard wiper arms. The accused product also includes a transverse baffle (model S950) or a pair of centrally connected protrusions (models S850, S851) in the interior front of the safety buckle. When the safety buckle is in the closed position, these baffles or protrusions abut the front of the wiper arm, preventing the wiper arm from moving forward and disengaging from the elastic element. The accused product does not fall within the scope of protection of claim 1.

(III) The original judgment erred in finding that the accused infringing product possessed the technical feature "said (elastic) element locks the connector in the inserted position within the front end of the wiper arm." 1. The term "lock" used in claim 1 of the patent-in-suit in "said (elastic) element locks the connector in the inserted position within the front end of the wiper arm" and "said safety buckle extends facing said locking element (i.e., elastic element), to prevent elastic deformation of said locking element and lock the connector" should be equivalent. The elastic element of the accused product can only "position" the connector in the inserted position within the front end of the wiper arm, but cannot "lock" it; the connector can be locked only when the safety buckle is in the closed position. 2. The original judgment's finding above was based on the accused product operating under the use environment of a standard wiper arm and a standard connector. When the accused product is used with a non-standard wiper arm, the elastic element cannot possibly "lock" the connector in the inserted position within the front end of the wiper arm.

(IV) The original judgment erred in finding that only the description in paragraph [0056] of the specification of the patent-in-suit should be used to define the functional technical feature of "used to prevent elastic deformation of the locking element and lock the connector." Only the specific manner of extending facing the locking element described in paragraph [0056] of the specification of the patent-in-suit can achieve the said function. Therefore, the technical features indispensable for achieving that function include the inner surface (reference numeral 77) of the vertical side wall of the safety buckle extending along (parallel to) the outer surface of the locking element, preventing the locking element from deforming transversely outward of the connector. From reference numeral 77, the inner surface of the safety buckle has a pair of protrusions parallel to the vertical side walls of the safety buckle.

(V) The original judgment erred in finding that the safety buckle of the accused infringing product extends facing the locking element when in the closed position. When determining that the safety buckle of the patent-in-suit extended facing the locking element, the original judgment used the concept that the safety buckle as a whole is located directly in front, with a part (inner surface) extending along the outer surface of the claw. When determining that the safety buckle of the accused product extended facing the locking element, the original judgment used the concept that a part of the safety buckle (the front part) is located directly in front, with a part (the two side walls) being parallel to the claw. The safety buckle of the accused product, as a whole, clearly does not extend facing the locking element but rather encloses and contains the locking element; locally, it does not extend facing the locking element either, but extends perpendicular to the locking element. The method of comparison used in the original judgment was erroneous and improperly expanded the scope of protection of the patent-in-suit.

(VI) The original judgment erred in finding that the technical means of the accused infringing product, which uses vertical protrusions on the safety buckle perpendicular to the claws of the locking element to limit the elastic opening of the locking element, with the vertical protrusions being located on the inner surfaces of both side walls of the safety buckle, is essentially the same as the technical means of the patent-in-suit, which uses the inner surface of the safety buckle parallel to the claws of the locking element to directly limit the locking element, and that their functions and effects are the same. 1. In the patent-in-suit, the safety buckle as a whole faces the locking element, and a part (the inner surface protrusions) extends parallel for locking. In contrast, in the accused product, the safety buckle as a whole encloses and contains the locking element, and a part (the front inner surface protrusions) extends perpendicular for locking. The technical means used are not substantially the same. 2. The effect of the accused product's safety buckle enclosing and containing the locking element as a whole is significantly better than the effect of the safety buckle in the patent-in-suit being located directly in front of the locking element as a whole; the effect achieved by the accused product's perpendicular extension locking is significantly better than the effect of the patent-in-suit's parallel extension locking. These distinguishing features would require inventive effort by a person of ordinary skill in the art at the time of the accused infringing act to conceive.

(VII) The original judgment erred in finding that Lucas Company and Fuke Company jointly committed the act of manufacturing the accused infringing products.

During the hearing of this appeal, Lucas Company and Fuke Company explicitly abandoned the appeal ground mentioned in (VII) above.

Valeo Company argued: The appeal grounds of Lucas Company and Fuke Company that the accused infringing product does not fall within the scope of protection of claim 1 of the patent-in-suit are untenable.

(I) Regarding the use environment feature of "a connector for a wiper, used to ensure the connection and articulation between a wiper arm and a component of a wiper blade." 1. From the literal meaning of the claim, the connection and articulation between the wiper arm and the wiper blade component are accomplished through an independent component, the connector. It clearly does not require direct contact between the wiper arm and the wiper blade component. 2. This literal meaning is verified by the embodiments in the specification of the patent-in-suit. 3. The parent application of the patent-in-suit contains consistent descriptions regarding the connector being used for connection and articulation as those in the specification of the patent-in-suit. Since the accused product also uses a connector to accomplish the connection and articulation between the wiper arm and the wiper blade component, it possesses the said use environment feature.

(II) Regarding the technical feature "and comprising at least one elastically deformable element, said element locking the connector in the inserted position within the front end of the wiper arm." 1. Claim 1, the specification, and the prosecution history of the patent-in-suit do not limit the technical solution to use only with a "standard wiper arm." 2. The accused product can be used in the use environment defined by the use environment feature in claim 1. Lucas Company and Fuke Company also acknowledged this. Furthermore, use in the use environment defined by claim 1 is the only reasonable commercial use for the accused product. Lucas Company and Fuke Company's allegation that the accused product can be used with non-standard wiper arms of smaller width is unfounded. According to the product introduction by Lucas Company and Fuke Company, the minimum wiper arm widths compatible with models S850, S851, and S950 are 7.8mm, 7.8mm, and 8.7mm, respectively. Upon measurement, the width of the locking claw of the connector of the accused product does not exceed 7mm. Therefore, in actual application, the accused product cannot be used with a wiper arm whose width is smaller than the inner diameter of the locking element. Furthermore, if the wiper arm width is smaller, shaking will inevitably occur after installation, leading to uneven wiping. Such unstable installation is clearly commercially and technically undesirable.

(III) Regarding the technical feature "said connector is locked in the inserted position within the wiper arm by a safety buckle." 1. According to the introduction of the accused product by Lucas Company and Fuke Company, the connector's size matches that of the wiper arm, and the connector can be locked in the inserted position within the wiper arm by the safety buckle. 2. Consumers will only purchase wipers compatible with their vehicle model; therefore, the connector can naturally be locked in the inserted position within the wiper arm by the safety buckle.

(IV) Regarding the technical feature "said safety buckle extends facing said locking element, to prevent elastic deformation of said locking element and lock the connector."

1. Regarding whether the safety buckle extends facing as a whole or partially. The shape of the safety buckle is not an indispensable technical feature for achieving the locking function. Whether the safety buckle faces the connector as a whole or partially, as long as a part of it extends facing the locking element, it can achieve the locking function and possesses the said technical feature. 2. Regarding the inner surface side walls. The indispensable technical feature for achieving the locking function is that the safety buckle extends facing the locking element. Under the premise of satisfying this indispensable technical feature, the specific shape of the inner surface side walls of the safety buckle does not affect the realization of the locking function. Furthermore, whether the interior of the safety buckle extends perpendicularly or parallelly towards the locking element, as long as there is spatial overlap with the locking element, it can prevent its deformation. Perpendicular extension and parallel extension constitute the same technical solution. 3. Regarding the front baffle. The accused product additionally includes a baffle or a pair of centrally connected protrusions at the front of the connector. This added technical feature cannot change the infringement determination result. Moreover, the accused product cannot realistically be used with a wiper arm of smaller width.

In conclusion, Valeo Company requests this Court to dismiss the appeal and affirm the original judgment. At the same time, as new evidence shows that the accused infringing act is continuing, Valeo Company requests this Court to support its application for an in-suit preservation of conduct, ordering Lucas Company and Fuke Company to immediately cease infringing the patent-in-suit.

Valeo Company's claims at the court of first instance included: an order for Lucas Company, Fuke Company, and Chen Shaoqiang to immediately cease the infringing acts, i.e., Lucas Company and Fuke Company to immediately cease manufacturing, selling, and offering for sale the accused infringing products, and Chen Shaoqiang to immediately cease manufacturing and selling the accused infringing products; an order for Lucas Company, Fuke Company, and Chen Shaoqiang to destroy the manufactured accused infringing products and related physical items and materials such as equipment, molds, and drawings used for manufacturing the accused infringing products; an order for Lucas Company, Fuke Company, and Chen Shaoqiang to jointly and severally pay compensation preliminarily set at 5,000,000 yuan and reasonable expenses incurred in stopping the infringing act preliminarily set at 1,000,000 yuan; and an order for Lucas Company, Fuke Company, and Chen Shaoqiang to bear all litigation costs and preservation fees of this case. During the first instance proceedings, Valeo Company requested the court of first instance to confirm that the accused infringing wiper products of models S850, S851, and S950 fell within the scope of protection of claims 1-10 of the patent-in-suit, and to render a preliminary judgment ordering Lucas Company, Fuke Company, and Chen Shaoqiang to immediately cease infringing the patent-in-suit.

The court of first instance found the following facts: Valeo Company is the patentee of the invention patent titled "Connector for a Vehicle Wiper and Corresponding Connecting Device," which is still within its term of protection. The claims of the patent are: "1. A connector for a wiper, used to ensure the connection and articulation between a wiper arm and a component of a wiper blade, said connector being fitted longitudinally from the rear to the front within the rearward longitudinally curved U-shaped front end of said wiper arm, and comprising at least one elastically deformable element

——said element locks the connector in an inserted position in the front end of the wiper arm, and includes two longitudinal vertical side edges configured to be received between two side flanks of a component of the wiper blade body; said connector is characterized in that the connector is locked in the inserted position in the wiper arm by a safety clasp, the safety clasp is movably mounted between a closed position and an open position, in the closed position, the safety clasp extends opposite the locking element, for preventing elastic deformation of the locking element, and locking the connector, while the open position allows the connector to be released from the wiper arm.

2. The wiper connector according to claim 1, characterized in that the safety clasp is movably mounted relative to the component of the wiper blade body.

3. The wiper connector according to claim 2, characterized in that the safety clasp is hingedly mounted relative to the component of the wiper blade body.

4. The wiper connector according to claim 3, characterized in that the safety clasp is hingedly mounted about a vertical axis of the component of the wiper blade body.

5. The wiper connector according to claim 4, characterized in that the hinge axis of the safety clasp is located at the longitudinal front end of one side flank of the component.

6. The wiper connector according to any one of claims 2 to 5, characterized in that the safety clasp is held in the closed position by a snap-fit structure of complementary shapes.

7. The wiper connector according to any one of claims 1 to 5, characterized in that the locking element is a claw, the claw extends forward freely and longitudinally from the longitudinal front end of one side edge of the connector, and its free end has a beveled or bird-beak shape, the beveled or bird-beak shape extends laterally inward of the connector, and, when the connector is in the inserted position, extends opposite the front surface of the longitudinal front end of the wiper arm.

8. The wiper connector according to claim 7, characterized in that the safety clasp forms a protective cover, the protective cover in the closed position extends opposite the outer surface of the free end of the locking claw of the connector.

9. The wiper according to any one of claims 1 to 5, characterized in that the clasp prevents the locking claw from deforming laterally outward of the connector, thereby ensuring that the connector cannot be dislodged beyond the front end of the wiper arm.

10. A connecting device for connecting a wiper blade body to a wiper arm, characterized in that it comprises a connector according to any one of claims 1 to 9 and a component plugged onto the wiper blade body.

Paragraph [0006] of the specification of the patent in suit states: "The locking of the connector position is generally ensured by an elastically deformable element. However, the wiper blade body may be violently pushed under the action of an impact. The strength of the locking element is insufficient, thus it deforms. It can no longer guarantee its locking function, which may cause the connector to come out accidentally, and for the same reason, the wiper blade body disengages from the wiper arm." Paragraph [0011] states: "Therefore, the object of the present invention is to propose a device for fixing the connector to a component of the wiper blade body, which device can lock the connector in the installed position, and can mount any type of wiper on a standard arm and a standard connector." Paragraph [0055] states: "The clasp is a plastic injection molded hollow element in the shape of a cover. It rotates about a vertical axis of the component, and is also movably mounted between a closed position and an open position, in the open position locking the connector in the inserted position within the hook-shaped end shown in Figure 2, and in the open position releasing the connector." Paragraph [0056] states: "The locking of the connector is ensured by the inner surface of the vertical side wall of the clasp, which inner surface extends along the outer surface of the claw. Therefore, the clasp prevents the claw from deforming laterally outward of the connector, so the connector cannot be released from the hook-shaped end."

The accused infringing products in this case are three models of motor vehicle wipers: S850, S851, and S950, each consisting of a wiper blade body, a connector, and a safety clasp. The connector is hingedly mounted on the base of the wiper blade body; the connector can connect the wiper arm and the wiper blade body. After connection, the wiper arm can rotate together with the connector about the horizontal axis on the base of the wiper blade body. The connector has two outwardly extending or projecting side edges forming a pair of elastically deformable elements, which side edges are located between the two side flanks of the base of the wiper blade body. The ends of the elastic elements are bent laterally inward (for models S850 and S851) or have protrusions (for model S950) toward the interior of the connector, which can snap into and confine the front bent portion of the wiper arm in the assembled connection position, i.e., the inserted position. Above the connector, there is a safety clasp, the rear portion of which is hingedly mounted on the wiper base, and can be rotated to close or open about the horizontal axis defined by the hinge point. The connector ensures that the safety clasp is held in the closed position by a snap-fit structure of complementary shapes. The inner surfaces of the two side walls of the safety clasp are provided with a pair of protrusions perpendicular to the side walls. When the safety clasp is in the closed position, the front portion of the safety clasp is located in front of the elastic elements, enclosing and sealing the elastic elements. The protrusions inside the side walls of the safety clasp correspond to the outer surfaces of the elastic elements and limit their elastic opening, thereby being able to lock the elastic elements and prevent the wiper arm from coming out of the elastic elements. A transverse baffle (for model S950) or a pair of interconnected protrusions (for models S850 and S851) are also provided inside the front of the safety clasp. When the safety clasp is in the closed position, the transverse baffle or protrusions are located in front of the wiper arm.

The court of first instance held that: In this case, it may first determine whether the accused infringing products fall within the scope of protection of claims 1-10 of the patent in suit, and supported Valeo Company's request for a partial judgment to be rendered first. The parties confirmed that the accused infringing products possess the additional technical features of claims 2, 3, and 6-10 of the patent in suit. The main dispute focused on whether the accused infringing products possess the three technical features of claim 1 of the patent in suit and the additional technical features of claims 4 and 5.

(I) Whether the accused infringing products possess the technical feature of claim 1: "A wiper connector for ensuring the connection and articulation between a wiper arm and a component of a wiper blade body." The court of first instance held that the above technical feature is an environmental use feature of the patent in suit. Claim 1 of the patent in suit does not limit the wiper arm to be a "standard wiper arm." The accused infringing products are motor vehicle wipers, which are connected to the wiper arm through the connector. The wiper arm can rotate together with the connector about the horizontal axis on the base of the wiper blade body. This connection mode should be recognized as articulation. The accused infringing products can be used in the environment defined by the environmental use feature of claim 1, thus satisfying said environmental use feature.

(II) Whether the accused infringing products possess the technical feature of claim 1: "and comprising at least one elastically deformable element — said element locks the connector in an inserted position in the front end of the wiper arm." The court of first instance held that the inward bends (for models S850 and S851) or protrusions (for model S950) at the ends of the pair of elastic elements of the accused infringing products can snap into the front bent portion of the wiper arm, thereby confining it in the assembled connection position, i.e., the inserted position. Under the action of a small external force, it is not easy to remove. It should be recognized that the elastic element can lock the connector in the inserted position in the front end of the wiper arm, thus the accused infringing products possess the above technical feature of the patent in suit.

(III) Whether the accused infringing products possess the technical feature of claim 1: "the connector is locked in the inserted position in the wiper arm by a safety clasp... in the closed position, the safety clasp extends opposite the locking element, for preventing elastic deformation of the locking element, and locking the connector." The court of first instance held that the above technical feature only discloses the direction and positional relationship between the safety clasp and the locking element, i.e., the elastic element. This directional relationship is insufficient to prevent elastic deformation of the locking element. A person of ordinary skill in the art, upon reading the claim alone, cannot directly and clearly determine the technical solution for achieving the function of "preventing elastic deformation of the locking element, and locking the connector." Therefore, the above technical feature is a functional feature. Only the content in paragraph [0056] of the specification of the patent in suit, that "the locking of the connector is ensured by the inner surface of the vertical side wall of the clasp, which inner surface extends along the outer surface of the claw, therefore, the clasp prevents the claw from deforming laterally outward of the connector, so the connector cannot be released from the hook-shaped end," constitutes the indispensable technical feature for achieving this function. This part should be used to define the functional technical feature. When the safety clasp of the patent in suit is closed, its entirety is located directly in front of the pair of locking elements, facing the locking elements as a whole; the locking of the connector is ensured by the inner surfaces of the vertical side walls of the safety clasp. The inner surfaces of the vertical side walls of the safety clasp fit against and snap over the outer surfaces of the locking elements, extending along the outer surfaces of the claws of the locking elements, thereby limiting the lateral outward deformation of the locking elements, thus performing the function of locking the connector. Although the safety clasp of the accused infringing products is not entirely positioned directly in front of the pair of locking elements in the closed position, its front portion encloses and seals the locking elements, and the front portion of the safety clasp is also directly in front of the locking elements. The two side walls of the safety clasp are also parallel to the two claws of the locking elements. It can be recognized that the safety clasp extends opposite the locking elements. The inner surfaces of the two side walls of the safety clasp of the accused infringing products are provided with a pair of protrusions perpendicular to the side walls. When the safety clasp is in the closed position, the positions of the protrusions correspond to the outer surfaces of the claws of the locking elements and limit their elastic opening, thereby being able to lock the connector. Both the accused infringing products and the patent in suit prevent the claws from deforming laterally outward of the connector by having the two vertical side walls of the safety clasp correspond to the outer surfaces of the claws of the locking elements. The technical means adopted are substantially the same, and the functional effects in preventing elastic deformation of the locking elements and locking the connector are also the same. Moreover, it is a technical solution that a person of ordinary skill in the art could conceive at the time of the alleged infringing act without creative work. Therefore, the accused infringing products possess technical features equivalent to the above technical features of the patent in suit.

(IV) Whether the accused infringing products possess the additional technical features of claims 4 and 5 of the patent in suit. The court of first instance held that the corresponding technical features of the accused infringing products are neither identical nor equivalent to the additional technical features of claims 4 and 5 of the patent in suit, and thus do not fall within the scope of protection of claims 4 and 5. In summary, the accused infringing products fall within the scope of protection of claims 1-3 and 6-10 of the patent in suit, but not within claims 4 and 5. Lucas Company and Fuke Company engaged in acts of selling, offering for sale, and jointly manufacturing the accused infringing products, and should bear civil liability for cessation of infringement. However, the existing evidence in this case cannot prove that Chen Shaoqiang committed acts of manufacturing or selling the accused infringing products.

In conclusion, the court of first instance ordered: Lucas Company and Fuke Company shall immediately cease infringing the patent right of the invention in suit from the effective date of the judgment.

During the second instance of this court, the parties submitted evidence in support of their appeal requests. This court organized the parties to exchange evidence and conduct cross-examination. Lucas Company and Fuke Company submitted two pieces of evidence: Evidence 1, "China Automotive Industry Standard · Motor Vehicle Windshield Electric Wiper Types and Dimensions (QC/T 46-92)," used to prove that hook-type wiper arms come in two widths, 9mm and 7mm (tolerance 0 to 0.1mm), and that other types and dimensions may be used if specially required, as agreed by the supplier and buyer; Evidence 2, U.S. Patent No. US005611103A and its Chinese translation, used to prove that prior connectors could not accommodate hook-type wiper arms of different sizes, and that the purpose of the U.S. patent was to accommodate three different widths of wiper arms, thereby demonstrating that the patent in suit can only accommodate a wiper arm with a width adapted to the locking element of the connector, whereas the accused infringing products can accommodate wiper arms not adapted to the width of the connector locking element. Valeo Company expressed its opinions on the two pieces of evidence, acknowledging their authenticity but arguing that neither is relevant to this case and that they cannot achieve Lucas Company and Fuke Company's purpose of proof. For the above evidence submitted by Lucas Company and Fuke Company, combined with Valeo Company's cross-examination opinions, this court makes the following certification: The authenticity of Evidence 1 and Evidence 2 can be confirmed, but they lack sufficient relevance to the interpretation of the claims and the infringement determination in this case, and are thus not admitted.

Valeo Company submitted two notarized documents: Notarial Deeds (2019) Hu Dong Zheng Jing Zi No. 2263 and No. 2340 issued by Shanghai Oriental Notary Public Office, used to prove that after the judgment of the first instance, the "CARALL Carl JD Self-Operated Flagship Store" was still selling the accused infringing products. Lucas Company and Fuke Company acknowledged the authenticity of the two notarial deeds and confirmed that the product attached to the notarial deeds is the accused infringing S851 model product in this case. At the same time, Lucas Company and Fuke Company claimed that they had already stopped the production and sale of the accused infringing products, that the S851 model product was exclusively supplied for JD.com's self-operated sales, and that the product purchased by Valeo Company through notarization should be from JD.com's inventory. Valeo Company acknowledged that the accused infringing S851 model product in this case was exclusively supplied for JD.com, and also acknowledged that the "carall flagship store" on Tmall had stopped selling the accused infringing products. For the above evidence submitted by Valeo Company, combined with the cross-examination opinions of Lucas Company and Fuke Company, this court makes the following certification: Lucas Company and Fuke Company have no objection to the authenticity of the two notarial deeds, and the facts they prove are relevant to this case and are thus admitted.

This court, upon trial, confirms that the facts found by the court of first instance are accurate.

This court further finds:

(I) Concerning the specification of the patent in suit. Paragraph [0043] of the specification of the patent in suit states: "The rod ensures that the connector is hingedly mounted on the wiper blade body about the transverse axis 'T1'." Paragraph [0044] states: "After the connector is fitted onto the rod, the wiper arm is mounted to this subassembly according to a known design, the hook-shaped end being inserted longitudinally from front to back into the skeleton of the connector, with the parallel lateral surfaces of the rod located between the side plates of the connector." Figures 1 and 3 of the specification clearly show the connection and articulation between the wiper arm and a part of the wiper blade body through the connector.

(II) Concerning the accused infringing products and acts. The "Common Problems with Wiper Blades" on the outer packaging of the accused infringing S851 model product in this case states: "If trembling occurs, replace the wiper immediately." Lucas Company and Fuke Company have stopped selling the accused infringing product on the "carall flagship store" on Tmall. Valeo Company, during the second instance, purchased the accused infringing S851 model product through notarization from the "CARALL Carl JD Self-Operated Flagship Store." This product is exclusively supplied for JD.com, and JD.com, in a self-operated manner, was still selling the accused infringing S851 model product.

(III) Concerning the opinions of the expert assistant. During the second instance hearing, Valeo Company applied for Mr. Tian Weichao, R&D Director of the company's Asia Pacific Wiper System R&D Center, to appear as an expert assistant to provide opinions on the factors to be considered in the design of motor vehicle wipers. Lucas Company and Fuke Company examined Mr. Tian. Mr. Tian opined that important considerations in the design of motor vehicle wipers are safety and compliance. In terms of safety, product design must ensure the adaptation and secure connection of all wiper components, including the wiper arm and the connector. When the wiper arm is not adapted to the connector, wobbling may occur, affecting not only the wiping effect but also causing driving safety hazards. Mr. Tian's opinions are objective and reasonable, and Lucas Company and Fuke Company did not deny the reasonableness of Mr. Tian's opinions. This court will consider the above opinions when evaluating the relevant issues.

(IV) Concerning the application for preliminary injunction during litigation. During the first instance of this case, Valeo Company filed an application with the court of first instance for a preliminary injunction during litigation ordering Lucas Company, Fuke Company, and Chen Shaoqiang to cease infringing the patent right of the invention in suit, and provided a cash bond of RMB 1,000,000. The court of first instance has not yet ruled on Valeo Company's application for a preliminary injunction during litigation. During the second instance, Valeo Company insisted on its application for a preliminary injunction during litigation ordering Lucas Company and Fuke Company to cease infringing the patent right of the invention in suit, and requested this court to support it.

This court holds that, based on the parties' appeal requests, responses, and the facts of the case, there are two main issues in dispute in the second instance: First, whether the accused infringing products fall within the scope of protection of claim 1 of the patent in suit; Second, how to handle the application for a preliminary injunction during litigation in this case.

I. Whether the accused infringing products fall within the scope of protection of claim 1 of the patent in suit

Lucas Company and Fuke Company appealed, arguing that the accused infringing products do not fall within the scope of protection of claim 1 of the patent in suit, and elaborated specific reasons for why the accused infringing products do not possess the three disputed technical features of claim 1 of the patent in suit. In this regard, this court analyzes as follows:

(A) Whether the accused infringing products possess the technical feature: "A wiper connector for ensuring the connection and articulation between a wiper arm and a component of a wiper blade body"

Lucas Company and Fuke Company appealed, arguing that in the accused infringing products, the wiper arm is connected to the connector, and the connector is articulated to the wiper blade body component; the wiper arm and the wiper blade body component do not directly contact each other and have no articulation relationship. Moreover, the connector of the patent in suit must connect to a "standard wiper arm," while the accused infringing products can also be used with non-standard wiper arms. Therefore, they do not possess the above technical feature of claim 1 of the patent in suit. In this regard, this court analyzes as follows:

First, regarding the interpretation of the technical feature "ensuring the connection and articulation between a wiper arm and a component of a wiper blade" among the above technical features. Article 59 of the Patent Law of the PRC stipulates that "the scope of protection of an invention patent shall be determined by the content of the patent claims, and the description and drawings may be used to interpret the content of the claims." Accordingly, the interpretation of patent claims and specific terms therein should be based on the content of the patent claims, in conjunction with the description and drawings, from the perspective of a person of ordinary skill in the art, and should not be taken out of context or distorted by separating them from the description and drawings. First, from the literal description of the above technical feature in the patent claim in question, it defines that the connector is used to ensure the connection and articulation between the wiper arm and the wiper blade component, but does not limit the wiper arm and the wiper blade component to direct contact. Second, the description and drawings of the patent in question also indicate that direct contact between the connector and the wiper blade component is not necessary. The textual descriptions in paragraphs [0043] and [0044] of the description of the patent in question, as well as the illustrations in Figures 1 and 3, all show that the wiper arm is connected to the connector, and the connector is articulated with the wiper blade component, thereby ensuring the connection and articulation between the wiper arm and the wiper blade component through the connector. This further confirms that the above technical feature in claim 1 of the patent in question does not require direct contact between the wiper arm and the wiper blade component.

Second, regarding whether the above technical feature should be interpreted as requiring that it must or can only be used to connect a standard wiper arm. First, with respect to the interpretation of the use environment feature. The subject matter protected by the patent in question is "a connector for a wiper," but the above technical feature does not directly define the structure of the connector; rather, it defines the connection relationship between the connector and other components, namely the wiper arm and the blade component, which effectively defines the environment in which the connector is used, and thus constitutes a use environment feature. The degree of limitation that a use environment feature imposes on the protected subject matter should be determined on a case-by-case basis. Generally, a use environment feature should be interpreted as requiring only that the protected subject matter can be used in that use environment, and not that the protected subject matter can only be used in that use environment; however, an exception exists where a person of ordinary skill in the art, after reading the patent claims, the description, and the patent examination file, can clearly and reasonably understand that the protected subject matter can only be used in that use environment. Second, this use environment feature cannot be interpreted to mean that the connector protected by the patent in question can only be used to connect a standard wiper arm. The patent claim in question does not state that the connector protected by the patent in question can only be used to connect a standard wiper arm. Although the description of the patent in question mentions, in the context of the invention's objective, that "any type of wiper can be installed on a standard arm and a standard connector," it does not exclude connecting a non-standard wiper arm. Furthermore, the above statement is only part of the invention's objective; the invention objective of the patent in question also includes "proposing a device for fixing the connector on a component of the wiper blade, said device being capable of locking the connector in the installation position." From the technical problem solved by the invention and the proposed technical solution, a person of ordinary skill in the art can fully understand that, as long as the width of the connector protected by the patent in question is compatible with the wiper arm, the technical solution of the patent in question can lock the connector in the installation position, and it is not necessary that it can only connect a standard wiper arm.

Third, regarding whether the accused infringing product possesses the above use environment feature. First, Lucas Company and Fuke Company acknowledged that the connector of the accused infringing product is connected to the wiper arm, and the connector and the wiper blade component are articulated. This in itself means that the accused infringing product achieves the connection and articulation between the wiper arm and the wiper blade component through the connector. At the same time, the connection and articulation relationships among the connector, the wiper arm, and the wiper blade component in the accused infringing product are no different from those disclosed in the description and corresponding drawings of the patent in question. Second, as previously stated, the above use environment feature of the patent in question cannot be interpreted to mean that the protected connector can only be used to connect a standard wiper arm. Article 9 of the Interpretation (II) of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Patent Infringement Dispute Cases stipulates: "If the accused infringing technical solution cannot be applied to the use environment defined by the use environment feature in the claim, the people's court shall determine that the accused infringing technical solution does not fall within the scope of protection of the patent right." Accordingly, as long as the accused infringing product can be used in the use environment defined by the use environment feature in the patent claim, it possesses that use environment feature; whether the accused infringing product can also be used in other use environments does not, in principle, affect the outcome of the infringement determination. Therefore, when the accused infringing product can achieve the connection and articulation between the wiper arm and the wiper blade component, whether the accused infringing product can also be used to connect a non-standard wiper arm has no substantial impact on the outcome of the infringement determination in this case.

In summary, the accused infringing product possesses the technical feature of "a connector for a wiper, which is used to ensure the connection and articulation between a wiper arm and a component of a wiper blade." The corresponding grounds of appeal by Lucas Company and Fuke Company are untenable and are not supported.

(2) Regarding whether the accused infringing product possesses the technical feature of "and comprising at least one elastically deformable element, said element locking the connector in an inserted position in the front end portion of the wiper arm"

Lucas Company and Fuke Company appealed, arguing that the term "locking" used in different places in claim 1 of the patent in question should be equivalent, and that the elastic element of the accused infringing product can only "position" the connector in the inserted position in the front end portion of the wiper arm, and cannot "lock" it. In this regard, this Court analyzes as follows:

First, regarding the interpretation of the term "locking" in the above technical feature. First, as previously stated, the interpretation of claims should be based on the understanding of a person of ordinary skill in the art after reading the description and drawings, and must not depart from the context of the description. The technical problem to be solved by the patent in question is to reduce or prevent the connector of a motor vehicle wiper from accidentally coming out under external force. In this context, a person skilled in the art can understand that when the elastic element of the connector "locks" the connector in the inserted position in the front end portion of the wiper arm, this "locking" does not mean complete fixation, but rather only needs to play a certain blocking or limiting role. Second, although both "said element locking the connector in the inserted position in the front end portion of the wiper arm" and "the safety catch extends facing the locking element, for preventing elastic deformation of the locking element, and locking the connector" use the term "locking," this does not mean that the effects of "locking" in these two instances are identical. From the overall technical solution of the invention in question, a person of ordinary skill in the art can understand that the locking of the wiper connector is ensured by two aspects: first, the "locking" implemented by the elastic element of the connector, i.e., the elastic element of the connector "locks the connector in the inserted position in the front end portion of the wiper arm"; second, the further "locking" implemented by the safety catch, i.e., "the safety catch extends facing the locking element, for preventing elastic deformation of the locking element, and locking the connector." The combined effect of both is required to achieve the final "locking" of the connector, reducing or preventing accidental removal of the connector. Among them, the "locking" implemented by the safety catch is based on the "locking" implemented by the elastic element, serving as a further enhancement of the "locking" implemented by the elastic element, and its final locking effect is naturally superior to that of locking by the elastic element alone. Therefore, the effects brought about by the two instances of "locking" are obviously different and cannot be equivalent.

Second, regarding whether the accused infringing product possesses the above technical feature. First, the elastic element ends of the accused infringing S850 and S851 model products are bent transversely inward into the connector, and the elastic element ends of the S950 model product have protrusions on both sides, which can engage with the front curved portion of a wiper arm whose width matches that of the elastic element, and block and limit it in the assembly connection position, i.e., the inserted position, in the front end portion of the wiper arm. Second, as long as the elastic element of the accused infringing product can block and limit the connector in the inserted position in the front end portion of a wiper arm whose width matches that of the elastic element, it possesses the above technical feature of the patent claim in question. When the elastic element of the accused infringing product is connected to a wiper arm whose width does not match that of the elastic element, whether or not a "locking" effect can be achieved does not affect the outcome of the infringement determination in this case. Finally, the accused infringing product is practically difficult to use with a wiper arm whose width does not match the end width of its elastic element. The expert assistant of Valeo Company, Tian Weichao, pointed out that ensuring safety is an important design consideration for wipers; when the wiper arm and connector are not compatible, shaking will occur, affecting the wiping effect and potentially causing safety hazards. This opinion is reasonable. When the accused infringing product is used with a wiper arm whose end width does not match the width of its elastic element, especially when the wiper arm is narrower than the elastic element end, the installed wiper arm will inevitably shake during use, affecting the wiping effect. Such a situation should obviously be avoided. The outer packaging of the accused infringing S851 model product also clearly states: "If trembling occurs, replace the wiper immediately." Therefore, in actual application, the accused infringing product must be used with a wiper arm whose width matches its elastic element end.

In summary, the accused infringing product possesses the technical feature of "and comprising at least one elastically deformable element, said element locking the connector in an inserted position in the front end portion of the wiper arm." The corresponding grounds of appeal by Lucas Company and Fuke Company are untenable and are not supported.

(3) Regarding whether the accused infringing product possesses the technical feature of "in the closed position, the safety catch extends facing the locking element, for preventing elastic deformation of the locking element, and locking the connector"

From the grounds of appeal of Lucas Company and Fuke Company, it can be seen that they essentially argue that the above technical feature in claim 1 of the patent in question is a functional feature, that the first instance judgment erred in determining the technical features essential for achieving that function, and that the accused infringing product does not have a technical feature identical or equivalent to the above functional feature. In this regard, this Court analyzes as follows:

First, regarding whether the above technical feature is a functional feature. The first instance court determined that this technical feature is a functional feature, on the grounds that it only discloses the directional and positional relationship between the safety catch and the locking element, that this directional relationship is insufficient to prevent elastic deformation of the locking element, and that a person of ordinary skill in the art, merely by reading the claim, cannot directly and clearly determine the specific implementation for achieving the function of "preventing elastic deformation of the locking element and locking the connector." In this regard, this Court opines as follows: First, regarding the definition of a functional feature. Article 8 of the Interpretation (II) of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Patent Infringement Dispute Cases clearly defines functional features and the method for their infringement comparison. Paragraph 1 of this Article provides: "Functional features refer to technical features that limit structure, components, steps, conditions, or relationships therebetween, etc., by the function or effect they perform in the invention-creation, except where a person of ordinary skill in the art can directly and clearly determine the specific implementation for achieving the above function or effect merely by reading the claims." Paragraph 2 provides: "Compared with the technical features essential for achieving the function or effect mentioned in the preceding paragraph as described in the description and drawings, if the corresponding technical feature of the accused infringing technical solution achieves the same function and effect by substantially the same means, and a person of ordinary skill in the art can conceive of it without inventive efforts at the time of the allegedly infringing act, the people's court shall determine that the corresponding technical feature is identical or equivalent to the functional feature." According to this provision, a functional feature refers to a technical feature that does not directly define the specific structure, components, steps, conditions, or relationships therebetween of the invention's technical solution, but rather limits the structure, components, steps, conditions, or relationships therebetween by the function or effect they perform in the invention-creation. If a technical feature has already defined or implied a specific structure, component, step, condition, or relationship therebetween of the invention's technical solution, even if the technical feature also simultaneously defines the function or effect achieved, in principle, it does not fall within the category of functional features as referred to in the above judicial interpretation and should not be compared as a functional feature for infringement. Second, regarding whether the technical feature "in the closed position, the safety catch extends facing the locking element, for preventing elastic deformation of the locking element, and locking the connector" in claim 1 of the patent in question is a functional feature. The above technical feature actually defines the directional relationship between the safety catch and the locking element and implies a specific structure: "the safety catch extends facing the locking element." The role of this directional and structural relationship is "preventing elastic deformation of the locking element and locking the connector." Based on this directional and structural relationship, in conjunction with the description and drawings of the patent in question, particularly the statement in paragraph [0056] of the description that "the locking of the connector is ensured by the inner surfaces of the vertical side walls of the catch, the inner surfaces extending along the outer surfaces of the claws, so the catch prevents the claws from deforming laterally outward from the connector, and therefore the connector cannot be disengaged from the hook-shaped end," a person of ordinary skill in the art can understand that "the safety catch extends facing the locking element." When the distance between the extending portion and the outer surface of the locking element is sufficiently small, it can achieve the effect of preventing elastic deformation of the locking element and locking the connector. Thus, the technical feature "in the closed position, the safety catch extends facing the locking element, for preventing elastic deformation of the locking element, and locking the connector" is characterized by both defining a specific orientation and structure and defining the function of that orientation and structure. Only by combining the orientation and structure with the function they perform can the specific content of the orientation and structure be clearly determined. This type of "orientation or structure + functional description" technical feature, although it includes a description of function, is essentially still an orientation or structure feature, and is not a functional feature as referred to in the aforementioned judicial interpretation. Finally, it should be noted that although the parties did not object to the first instance court's determination that the above feature is a functional feature, the interpretation of claims is a question of law, and there are significant differences in the infringement comparison method between functional features and other types of technical features, which may affect the outcome of the infringement determination. Therefore, this Court specifically points this out and corrects it.

Second, regarding the comparison of technical features for infringement. The technical feature in claim 1 of the patent in question "in the closed position, the safety catch extends facing the locking element, for preventing elastic deformation of the locking element, and locking the connector" both defines the directional and structural relationship between the safety catch and the locking element and describes the function performed by the safety catch. This function has a limiting effect on determining the directional and structural relationship between the safety catch and the locking element. This technical feature is not a functional feature; both the directional/structural limitation and the functional limitation should be considered in the infringement determination. In this case, the inner surfaces of the two side walls of the safety catch of the accused infringing product are provided with a pair of protrusions perpendicular to the side walls. When the safety catch is in the closed position, the protrusions on the inner surfaces of its side walls face the outer surface of the elastic element, which can function to limit the elastic deformation and opening of the elastic element, lock the elastic element, and prevent the wiper arm from disengaging from the elastic element. When the safety catch of the accused infringing product is in the closed position, the protrusions on the inner surfaces of the two side walls perpendicular to the side walls face the outer surface of the elastic element, which is a form of "the safety catch extends facing the locking element" as referred to in claim 1 of the patent in question, and can also achieve the function of "preventing elastic deformation of the locking element, and locking the connector." Therefore, the accused infringing product possesses a technical feature identical to the technical feature of "in the closed position, the safety catch extends facing the locking element, for preventing elastic deformation of the locking element, and locking the connector." The first instance court, based on its determination that the above feature is a functional feature, found that the means of the accused infringing product (front portion containing the locking element plus local perpendicular extension locking) was equivalent to the means of the patent in question (overall facing the locking element plus local parallel extension locking), and thus determined that the accused infringing product possessed a technical feature equivalent to the above feature. Although the comparison method and conclusion were somewhat deviant, they did not affect the outcome of the infringement determination in this case.

Third, regarding the additional technical features of the accused infringing product. The accused infringing product's safety catch is also provided with a transverse baffle (S950 model) or a pair of centrally connected protrusions (S850, S851 models) at its inner front. When the safety catch is in the closed position, the transverse baffle or protrusions are located in front of the wiper arm. First, the above features are additional technical features of the accused infringing product. When the accused infringing product possesses all the technical features of the patent in question, the accused infringing product has already utilized the technical contribution of the patent in question. The additional technical features and the additional technical effects they produce do not have a substantial impact on the outcome of the patent infringement determination. Second, the superior technical effect claimed by Lucas Company and Fuke Company due to the additional technical features of the accused infringing product is difficult to sustain. If the connector of the accused infringing product is connected to a wiper arm whose width matches that of its elastic element, the forward movement of the wiper arm will be blocked by the inward bend or protrusion at the end of the elastic element, and the transverse baffle or protrusions at the inner front of the safety catch cannot perform a blocking function. Thus, the additional technical features do not actually produce the technical effect claimed by Lucas Company and Fuke Company. At the same time, if the connector of the accused infringing product is connected to a wiper arm narrower than the width of its elastic element, when the wiper arm moves forward, the inward bend or protrusion at the end of the elastic element cannot perform its locking function, and the transverse baffle or protrusions at the inner front of the safety catch may play a certain blocking role. However, as previously discussed, in such a case, because the width of the wiper arm is smaller than the width of the elastic element of the connector, shaking will inevitably occur during use, affecting the wiping effect, and this situation should be avoided.

In summary, the accused infringing product possesses the technical feature "at the closed position, the safety buckle extends facing the locking element to prevent elastic deformation of the locking element and to lock the connector." The court of first instance found the above feature to be a functional feature. Although its application of law was erroneous and its method of comparing technical features and conclusion deviated, this did not affect the outcome of the infringement determination in this case. Therefore, the accused infringing product falls within the scope of protection of claim 1 of the patent in suit, and the acts of Lucas Company and Fuke Company have infringed the patent in suit. Their corresponding grounds of appeal cannot be established and are not supported.

2. How should the preliminary injunction application in this case be handled?

During the first instance proceedings of this case, Valeo Company filed an application for a preliminary injunction to order Lucas Company, Fuke Company, and Chen Shaoqiang to cease infringing the patent in suit, and provided corresponding security. After the court of first instance rendered a partial judgment supporting the patentee's claim for cessation of infringement, it had not yet ruled on the preliminary injunction application, and that partial judgment entered the appeal proceedings. This Court analyzes the handling of Valeo Company's above-mentioned preliminary injunction application as follows:

(1) Regarding the jurisdiction over the preliminary injunction application in this case

Article 161 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "For cases where a party appeals a judgment of first instance, before the case is transferred to the people's court of second instance, if a party engages in conduct such as transferring, concealing, selling, or destroying property and a preservation measure must be taken, the people's court of first instance shall take the measure upon the party's application or ex officio. The preservation ruling of the people's court of first instance shall be promptly submitted to the people's court of second instance." By reference to the above provision, for cases where a party appeals the judgment of first instance, if a party files an application for a preliminary injunction during the first instance proceedings, before the case is transferred to the people's court of second instance, the people's court of first instance has jurisdiction; after the case is transferred to the people's court of second instance, the people's court of second instance shall have jurisdiction. In this case, since the case has already been accepted by this Court, the preliminary injunction application related to this case shall also be under the jurisdiction and handling of this Court.

(2) Regarding the specific handling of the preliminary injunction application in this case

The special circumstance that needs to be considered in this case is that although the court of first instance has rendered a partial judgment ordering cessation of infringement of the patent in suit, that judgment has not yet taken effect, and the patentee continues to insist on its preliminary injunction application from the first instance proceedings. Although this preliminary injunction application may overlap in content with the partial judgment ordering cessation of infringement, and its function is similar in that both aim to clarify the legal relationship status between the parties as soon as possible and improve the efficiency of dispute resolution, as two different institutional designs, the preliminary injunction application ordering cessation of infringement still has unique value in specific circumstances. For example, when there is an emergency situation where the applicant's interests are being infringed or other circumstances causing harm to the applicant, and the partial judgment ordering cessation of infringement has not yet taken effect because it is under appeal, the preliminary injunction measure ordering cessation of infringement during the proceedings can achieve the effect of promptly stopping the infringing conduct, thereby more effectively protecting the patent right. In particular, given the reality that China's relevant civil procedure laws do not provide for a temporary enforcement system for judgments that have not yet taken effect, the value of a preliminary injunction ordering cessation of infringement becomes even more evident. In view of this, when considering a preliminary injunction application for cessation of patent infringement, the people's court of second instance may consider the following circumstances and handle them separately: If there is an emergency or if other harm may be caused, and the patentee files a preliminary injunction application, but the people's court of second instance cannot render a final judgment within the time limit for handling the preliminary injunction application, it shall separately handle the preliminary injunction application and issue a ruling in a timely manner in accordance with the law; if the conditions for a preliminary injunction are met, it shall promptly take the preservation measure. At that time, since the judgment of first instance has already found infringement established, the people's court of second instance may review the preliminary injunction application based on the facts of the case, and security is not necessarily required. If the people's court of second instance can render a final judgment within the time limit for handling the preliminary injunction application, it may promptly render the judgment and reject the preliminary injunction application. In this case, Valeo Company insisted during the second instance proceedings on its preliminary injunction application to order Lucas Company and Fuke Company to cease infringing the patent in suit. However, the evidence submitted by Valeo Company is insufficient to prove that an emergency situation causing harm to it has occurred. Moreover, this Court has already rendered its judgment in court, and this judgment has taken legal effect. Making a separate ruling on a preliminary injunction ordering cessation of infringement of the patent in suit is no longer necessary. Therefore, Valeo Company's preliminary injunction application is not supported.

In summary, the appeal claims of Lucas Company and Fuke Company cannot be established and shall be dismissed. The judgment of first instance has clear findings of fact, and although the determination of functional features has a defect in the application of law, it does not affect the outcome of this case and shall be affirmed. Pursuant to Article 59 of the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 8 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Patent Infringement Dispute Cases (II), Item 1 of Paragraph 1 of Article 170 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 334 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows:

The appeal is dismissed and the original judgment is affirmed.

The appeal case acceptance fee of RMB 500 shall be borne jointly by Xiamen Lucas Auto Parts Co., Ltd. and Xiamen Fuke Auto Parts Co., Ltd.

This judgment is final. The parts of this case concerning damages for infringement and other matters shall continue to be tried by the court of first instance.
